election._note: Open-list proportional representation with a 5% threshold under the 2020 Electoral Code (the 2019 Rada was elected half by list, half in single-member districts). Elected 21 July 2019; the 2024 election was SUSPENDED under martial law, which the constitution forbids elections during, and no date exists. The game books October 2027 -- the AUTHOR'S CALL (2026-10-15), a plausible post-suspension date inside a first term, recorded as a bound rather than a forecast. This game draws no war (docs/tiers/v4.md refuses it); the suspension is the one trace it leaves here. Constitution of Ukraine, Arts. 76-77, 83; Electoral Code 2020.

dissolution._note: Art. 90: the President may terminate the Rada's powers if no coalition forms within a month, no cabinet within sixty days, or no plenary sits for thirty days -- conditioned discretion, read as the template's executive_discretion with a lockout; not within the Rada's first year or the President's last six months, and never under martial law. Constitution of Ukraine, Art. 90.

head_of_state._note: The President, directly elected for five years, two consecutive terms at most; commander-in-chief, nominates the defence and foreign ministers and the Prime Minister for the Rada's approval. Elected April 2019; the 2024 election was suspended under martial law. Constitution of Ukraine, Arts. 102-106.
head_of_state.title: President

executive._note: Booked March 2027 -- the AUTHOR'S CALL (2026-10-15), the same reasoning as the Rada's date above; two rounds, five-year term. Art. 103's two-consecutive-terms limit is recorded here and authored 0 below, CYP's convention. Constitution of Ukraine, Art. 103.
executive.title: President

amendment._note: Art. 155: a draft passes a preliminary majority of all deputies and then 300 of 450 -- two thirds -- at the next session; Chapters I, III and XIII additionally need a national referendum (Art. 156); no amendment may be made under martial law (Art. 157). The semi-presidential template carries three_fifths only, the lower bar recorded honestly as the template's. Constitution of Ukraine, Arts. 155-157.
amendment._referendum_note: Art. 156's referendum is mandatory for the entrenched chapters only -- a split the referendum field cannot carry. Constitution of Ukraine, Art. 156.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: Art. 157 forbids amendments that abolish or restrict rights or the state's independence and territorial integrity; the form of government itself was changed by the 2004 and 2014 amendments, so it is amendable.

judicial._note: A Constitutional Court reviews the constitutionality of laws (Arts. 147-153). Constitution of Ukraine, Art. 150.

formation._note: The Rada appoints the Prime Minister on the President's nomination, made on the coalition's proposal (Art. 114) -- the template's presidential_appointment. A no-confidence vote needs a majority of the Rada's constitutional composition, 226 (Art. 87), the template's absolute_members exactly. The current Prime Minister took office in July 2025. Constitution of Ukraine, Arts. 87, 114.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. The medieval Kingdom of Ruthenia is the nearest crown; the restored line here is fictional.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/Ministry of Finance ~2024, rounded, on AUT.json's conventions -- A WARTIME BUDGET, measured as it is: defence ~26% of GDP and expenditure near 65%, the gap financed by allied grants and loans that no field here carries. VAT 20%; corporate 18%; income 23 is the 18% personal rate plus the military levy (1.5% raised to 5% in December 2024); capital gains 18%; no wealth tax. Revenue ~36% of GDP includes the unified social contribution. Debt ~90% of GDP (end-2024). The AI nation's budget does not tick (V4.4), so these figures seed its standing and its trade, not a deficit spiral.
